headline.title: Video-generation startup PixVerse raises $439M, valuation soars past $2B
headline.summary: Video-generation startup PixVerse has raised $439 million in funding, bringing its valuation to over $2 billion. The company plans to use the investment to enhance its world model offerings and expand its customer base globally.

articles.title: Hermes agent maker Nous Research in talks for new funding at $1.5B valuation
articles.summary: Nous Research, a maker of Hermes agents, is in discussions to secure at least $75 million in new funding at a valuation of $1.5 billion, with Robot Ventures leading the round and participation from USV and other notable investors. The funding aims to support the company's growth and development in AI technology.

articles.title: New York becomes the first state to enact a data center moratorium
articles.summary: New York has enacted a one-year moratorium on new hyperscale data centers, making it the first state to implement such a measure, following Governor Kathy Hochul's approval. Additionally, a bill that could impose further restrictions on data center developments is pending her signature.

articles.title: Already rich, already successful, why the last wave of tech winners is grinding again
articles.summary: Recent tech industry leaders, already successful and wealthy, are re-engaging in the sector, driven by the potential of AI's transformative impact and the opportunity for significant financial gain. This renewed focus reflects a sense of urgency to capitalize on what many perceive as a pivotal moment in technology.

articles.title: Uber’s product chief on hotels, robotaxis, and why the company doesn’t want to be “everything for everyone”
articles.summary: Uber's Chief Product Officer Sachin Kansal discussed the company's focus on financial services, its evolving partnership with Waymo, and the establishment of new AV Labs for data operations. He emphasized that Uber aims to avoid becoming "everything for everyone" while integrating AI to enhance the experiences of riders and drivers.

articles.title: EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents
articles.summary: EvoCUA-1.5 introduces an online reinforcement learning framework for multi-turn computer-use agents, enabling them to effectively navigate and interact with complex desktop environments. This approach addresses the limitations of static imitation learning by allowing agents to adapt to dynamic changes in their environment through continuous learning and interaction.

articles.title: From Patterns to Maze Structures: SMT-Based Path Synthesis and 2D/3D Construction
articles.summary: Researchers have developed a pipeline for generating maze structures from various input patterns, utilizing Satisfiability Modulo Theories to encode path-synthesis problems with constraints on adjacency and coverage. The method allows for the creation of both planar and layered maze paths in a single computational step.

articles.title: Co4ICF: Co-evolving Physics-Informed Surrogate and RL-based Pulse Optimizer for Inertial Confinement Fusion
articles.summary: The article introduces Co4ICF, a novel framework that integrates a physics-informed surrogate model with a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based pulse optimizer to enhance the reliability of predictions in Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF). This approach addresses the challenge of offline-trained surrogates failing when inputs are driven into out-of-distribution regions by iteratively refining the surrogate based on policy-induced trajectories.

articles.title: Imaging-101: Benchmarking LLM Coding Agents on Scientific Computational Imaging
articles.summary: The article introduces Imaging-101, a benchmark consisting of 57 expert-verified computational imaging tasks across six scientific domains, aimed at improving the reconstruction pipeline in computational imaging. This resource is designed to assist domain scientists by providing structured tasks grounded in peer-reviewed research, addressing the challenges of building effective imaging solutions.

articles.title: SVR-R1: Bootstrapping Multi-modal Reasoning with Self-verification in Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: The Self-Verified Reasoner (SVR-R1) is a new multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that utilizes self-verification as a learning signal for multimodal reasoning. The model evaluates its own answers with a binary verdict, allowing for a second chance to rethink responses if necessary, thereby enhancing the learning process.

articles.title: HCRMap: Pressure-Aware Hot-Expert Residency Mapping for 3.5D MoE Chiplet Inference
articles.summary: The article presents HCRMap, a method designed to optimize the activation of experts in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models during inference on 3.5D multi-chiplet systems. By addressing the issue of expert hotness skew, HCRMap aims to improve compute balance and reduce pressure on communication, memory bandwidth, and execution resources.

articles.title: JEPA for AI-Native 6G: Predictive Representations and Open Challenges
articles.summary: The article discusses the transition of sixth-generation (6G) networks towards AI-native operations, emphasizing the integration of learning modules throughout the radio access network, edge, and core. It highlights the challenges posed by limited labels, heterogeneous data, and non-stationary conditions, proposing the joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) as a potential self-supervised solution to address these issues.
